description: The plot illustrates the training loss over iterations for different configurations of the SepLLM model, as described in the paper “SepLLM: Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into One Separator.” The x-axis, labeled “#Iteration,” spans from 95,000 to 125,000 in linear scale, with major tick marks every 5,000 iterations. The y-axis, labeled “Loss,” ranges from 2.0 to 3.0, also on a linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. Four distinct curves are shown: a pink solid line with circular markers representing “SepLLM (n=64, larger lr),” which starts near 3.0 at 95,000 iterations and steadily declines to approximately 2.22 by 125,000; a dark blue solid line with circular markers for “SepLLM (n=128),” beginning near 2.95 and decreasing to about 2.28; an orange solid line with circular markers for “SepLLM (n=64),” starting near 2.95 and ending around 2.29; and a red dashed horizontal line, likely representing a baseline or target loss, fixed at approximately 2.35 across all iterations. All three SepLLM variants exhibit a rapid initial drop in loss followed by a slower, gradual decline, with the “n=64, larger lr” configuration achieving the lowest final loss.
